answer.reason: The old harness prints only parser-produced trees. Parsing and printing start at depth zero and count nested arrays and objects against the same limit, so the new object print guard cannot reject an object at a parser-accepted depth. The harness also permits a null print result.

scope_contract.reason: Printing parser-produced objects is part of this entry's parse-to-print operation.

feasible_trigger.reason: No parser-produced object can reach the new guard at a rejected depth: parsing and both print routes begin at zero, and the container parsers reject that depth first.

observable_consequence.reason: The proposed depth-only print failure cannot occur on the harness route. Independently, this harness has no assertion requiring a non-null print result.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The ordinary parse-to-print route already reaches objects at every parser-accepted depth. Both buffered and unbuffered printing use that tree.

identity_preserved.reason: The same operation and condition—printing a parser-produced object at a parser-accepted depth—are compared before and after with the fixed harness.
